title: SDK adoption pathways & triage rubric for regulated customers
creator: Priya Singh
description: Goal: Define a repeatable intake + prioritization rubric and initial implementation plan for SDK/client library requests coming from regulated/enterprise customers. Scope focuses on three areas: language binding demand, auth patterns (SSO / short-lived tokens / token rotation / proxy patterns), and streaming ergonomics (resumable sessions, backpressure, client reconnection semantics). Deliverables: 1) a scoring rubric to prioritize requests; 2) an intake checklist for Sales/Support to capture required info; 3) a proposed minimal implementation plan for 2-3 high-priority SDKs; 4) security and compliance guardrails required before release to regulated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Triage rubric documented and reviewed with Eng/Design/Security
Intake form (single page) created for Sales/Support and linked from PRD
Top-3 language bindings selected with rough effort estimates and owners
Auth patterns matrix (SSO/OAuth, token rotation, key-proxy) validated by Security
Streaming ergonomics recommendations (resumable stream API, client backpressure guidance) prototyped in one SDK
Release gating checklist (privacy, KMS integration, logging audit) agreed and linked
tasks: Synthesize customer asks from last 12 months into canonical request types (owner: Jonas)
Draft scoring rubric with weights for Adoption Signal, Security Risk, Engineering Effort, Revenue Impact, and Maintenance Burden (owner: Priya)
Align with Security on required authentication/rotation patterns for regulated customers (owner: Sasha - Security)
Prototype resumable streaming helper in node-sdk to validate API surface and telemetry (owner: Eng - SDK team)
Work with Design to create API ergonomics doc for streaming and reconnection flows (owner: Alex - Design)
Publish intake form and run one intake shadow session with Sales for feedback (owner: GTM)
Prioritize first release languages and create GH epics for ENG-implementation
comments: 2025-03-04 Priya: Kickoff — compiled 28 incoming requests tagged as 'sdk' from CSM backlog. Initial theme buckets: language gaps, auth integration, streaming robustness.
2025-03-06 Jonas: Draft rubric posted. Proposed weights: Adoption 30, Security 25, Effort 20, Revenue 15, Maint 10. Request feedback from Security and Eng leads.
2025-03-07 Sasha (Security): We need a minimum spec for token lifetime and rotation. Will review OAuth PKCE + service-to-service exchange and blacklist long-lived API keys for regulated releases.
2025-03-09 Alex (Design): Sketches for resumable-stream API completed (resume token, sequence IDs, ack semantics). Will share with SDK engineers for feasibility.
2025-03-11 Jonas: Ran intake shadow with Sales — two enterprise prospects asked for C# and Java bindings + SSO plug-in. Both require FIPS-compliant TLS and audit logging in the SDK.

2025-03-12 Priya: Decision to fast-follow Python/Node as v1 SDK distribution; parallel design work for C# and Java templates. Security review flagged HSM/KMS mapping for private deployments; added to dependencies.
notes: Prioritize SDKs using telemetry + enterprise signal rather than purely open-source downloads. Suggested telemetry sources: signups, integration requests, paid contract mentions.
For streaming ergonomics prefer idempotent resume tokens and per-request sequence numbers to simplify server replay and debugging in multi-tenant environments.
Auth: prefer short-lived credentials with refresh via an exchange endpoint; provide a documented proxy pattern for customers who must keep secrets off client devices.
Consider shipping a 'micro-sdk' pattern: minimal thin HTTP wrapper with reference integrations in 4 languages instead of full-featured heavy clients initially.
Cost to maintain should be evaluated per-language; add a maintenance score threshold in the rubric to avoid low-usage SDK churn.
